rationale: Workload M=128,N=4096,K=4096; all listed block sizes divide dimensions, so the Cartesian product stays feasible. Previous selection (128,128,64,1) compiled with 186 registers and 32768B dynamic smem, giving blocks_per_sm=2 with one wave of 32 blocks; the simulator estimated tensor busy 0.88 but DRAM busy 0.65 and miss_frac 0.516, suggesting num_stages=1 leaves little latency-hiding headroom. I keep the same domains (threads fixed at 128; block_M up to 128 to reduce A-side traffic on the small M; block_N in {64,128}; block_K in {32,64}; stages 1-3) but shift weight away from launches (0.3) since a single wave already launches trivially, and slightly raise pipeline weight (0.6) and footprint (0.4) so the MIP is less likely to pick an under-pipelined variant that risks high DRAM stall fraction, while still honoring the 49152B cap (e.g. 128x128x32 st3 = 49152B fits; 128x128x64 st3 exceeds). Analytic features are normalized model quantities, not measured timings; simulator values are model estimates only. Feedback is compile/resource/simulation only: CPU-shadow pass, compilation success, dynamic smem, register count, and simulator instruction mix do NOT establish CUDA numerical correctness or GB10 performance, and no SASS-derived timing is claimed.
